summary.tldr: Requires finfish aquaculture off the Pacific Coast to use closed containment facilities and orders a transition plan for affected workers.
what_it_does: Defines a "closed containment facility" as a solid wall structure, onshore or offshore, that keeps fish, parasites, waste and other pollutants from escaping into surrounding marine systems.
Allows commercial finfish aquaculture licences off the Pacific Coast only if the fish are raised in a closed containment facility.
Bans finfish aquaculture in Canadian fisheries waters off the Pacific Coast unless it is done under that type of licence.
Phases in the ban for current licence holders, their existing licences can continue until they expire or until the fourth anniversary of the new rule, whichever comes first.

Requires the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, within 12 months, to table and implement a transition plan with support for affected corporations and workers, including training and income support through employment insurance.
summary.background: The bill amends the Fisheries Act. It applies to Canadian fisheries waters off the Pacific Coast.
